public_rationale: CoreWeave and Nebius disclosed large Meta contracts, which materially challenge the suggestion that no significant independent customers exist. But the full claim also says those customers cannot warrant the investment scale. Multiyear contract values alone cannot settle that comparison, and the post leaves the investment denominator and intended treatment of Meta unclear. A categorical contradiction would discard a material part of his wording.
limitations: The simpler claim that no large independent customers exist faces substantial contrary evidence.
Contract commitments are not realized revenue or proof of profitable investment.
The unknown financial basis prevents a definitive money score.

criteria.support_condition: Customer and project records show that demand outside the exclusions is too small to materially support the identified neocloud investment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent customers have commitments demonstrably large enough to support a material portion of the relevant capacity investment on comparable terms.

evidence.explanation: The announcement identifies an approximately $21 billion agreement through December 2032 supporting Meta's own AI operations. This challenges a literal absence of large independent customers, but does not establish returns on the relevant capital expenditure.

The agreement combines $12 billion of dedicated capacity with up to $15 billion of additional purchases tied to available capacity. It predates the target quarter and challenges the broad customer claim, but the maximum contract value is neither realized annual revenue nor proof that all investment is justified.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Identify the investment cohort and intended Meta exclusion, then match independent customer commitments, delivery schedules and project economics to that investment.
